title: Reinforcement of Wing Lower Cover Stringer Run-Outs Between Ribs 8 and 14, VANTOR-68

ata.title: Wing Box Structure — Lower Cover Panels

abstract: Local build-up of the lower cover panel at the stringer run-outs inboard of rib 14 on the four-engine VANTOR-68, where the higher wing bending spectrum of the stretched airframe eroded the fatigue margin predicted at certification.

sections.reason: Full-scale fatigue test evidence gathered after the extended service goal was agreed showed the stringer run-out region of the VANTOR-68 lower cover reaching its crack initiation life between 44 000 and 51 000 flight cycles rather than the 60 000 assumed. The VANTOR-68 carries a heavier wing bending spectrum than any other member of the family because of the fuselage stretch and the four-engine inertia relief distribution, so the finding does not transfer to the twin-engine aircraft. Two operators had by then passed 38 000 cycles and one had recorded a 9 mm indication at the rib 11 run-out during a scheduled ultrasonic survey.
sections.description: The run-out of stringers 12 through 18 on the lower cover, between ribs 8 and 14, is re-profiled from a stepped taper to a continuous tapered pad and a local bonded and bolted strap is added over the last three fastener rows. Stringer kit D5710124822382 is replaced by a machined item with the pad integral, and the lower spar cap kit D5710125087378 is re-drilled locally. The outboard skin panel assembly FA508915-80 is retained. Loop clamps EN26865-6B carrying the fuel quantity harness are relocated 40 mm inboard to clear the new pad. The work is done from inside the tank through the access panels of zones 531, 541 and 591, with the aircraft de-fuelled and the tank purged. Revised detail is on drawings D57101111565 and D57101380390. The sizing spectrum is the four-engine wing bending spectrum recovered from recorded flight data across the operating fleet, not the twin-engine spectrum.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 21 kg per aircraft, distributed symmetrically, with a centre-of-gravity shift below 0.03 per cent MAC. No electrical load change. Not interchangeable: the re-profiled stringer cannot be fitted to an unmodified spar cap because the fastener pitch of the last three rows changes. The recurring ultrasonic inspection of the run-out region at 6 000 flight cycles is removed once embodied, which is the main operator benefit. SRM allowable damage limits for the lower cover in this bay must be re-issued because the existing scheme assumes the stepped taper.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only; the VANTOR-68 production line closed before the change was ready. Embodiment is through Service Bulletin SLN-57-1021 during a scheduled 12-year check, preceded by the ultrasonic survey of SLN-57-1017. Tank entry, purge and re-sealing dominate the elapsed time; typical downtime is eleven days.

type_data.production_impact: None; the VANTOR-68 line is closed

The pad geometry is unchanged as a result, but the delta is now part of the substantiation record and any further aft limit movement has to be assessed against it.
